subject: AcmeApps — reliability comparison & next-test plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hayes <marcus@acmeapps.com>, procurement@acmeapps.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — reliability comparison & next steps

Hi Marcus / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really productive. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get a concrete reliability/interop comparison in your hands: 

Key notes from today's call
- Primary goals: quantify failover behavior, steady-state throughput per-dollar, and operational constraints (rate limits, error budget behavior).
- Baseline hyperscaler features you care about: region failover, per-tenant rate limits, and SLA-backed uptime.
- Your constraints: no more than 200ms p95 end-to-end for short prompts, 99.95% effective availability target, and transparent error budget signals to SRE.

What Redwood will demonstrate (proposed tests)
1) Sustained-load profile: 1k RPS for 30m on a representative 128-token generation workload (measure P50/P95/P99 latency, token throughput, and unit cost).
2) Spike/failover scenario: force a region-level outage for 5 minutes and observe routing to fallback region and model-variant fallback (measure failover time, request loss, and observed error budget burn).
3) Error-budget burn test: synthetic elevated error rate on a small percentage of traffic to validate alerting and automatic fallback triggers.
4) Cold start & scale: repeated scale-ups from idle to 500 RPS to capture cold-start latency distributions.
5) Rate-limit behavior: simulate bursty clients hitting per-API and per-key limits; verify retry semantics and throttling headers.

Deliverables we propose
- A test artifact pack (attached): 'slo-test-template.xlsx' with metric definitions and target pass/fail criteria.
- A competitive matrix we sketched comparing Redwood vs two leading hyperscalers on failover modes and required integration work (attached).
- A short failover demo runbook and artifacts for your SREs.

Timing
- Proposed test window: Tue Nov 17 or Thu Nov 19 (30–90 minute demo + 24–48 hour test execution). Which works for your SRE/infra folks?

Next ask from you
- Confirm which test window works and share a single technical contact on your side who can add the temporary test key/IP allowlist.

I copied Ben and Karthik to plan the engineering scope and confirm we can run the region-failover demo in our staging environment.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: slo-test-template.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf

From: Marcus Hayes <marcus@acmeapps.com>

Vanessa — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Uptime/SLA framing: your note said 99.95% — can you provide examples of what that looks like in terms of regional vs global coverage? Hyperscaler X will treat a regional outage as a partial SLA hit; we need to understand Redwood's failover windows for region vs cross-region.
2) Rate limits and retries: does Redwood expose per-key headers showing remaining quota? How aggressive are retries vs returning 429s? Our client libraries prefer bubble-up 429 for backoff.
3) Cost telemetry: we need an estimate of token-level cost for generation at 128 tokens under the sustained test so we can compare to our internal benchmarking.
4) Can you demonstrate a full region outage (not just a model instance failover) — we want to see request continuity to a different region for <2 minutes of disruption.

If you can include those points in the runbook and confirm required access (IP ranges, test keys) we'll confirm availability for Thu Nov 19.

Also loop in your SE to confirm whether we should expect any client-side changes to accept fallback model variants.

— Marcus
Marcus Hayes

Vanessa / team — here's a concise test plan and answers to Marcus' bullets. I kept the plan minimal so we can run it in staging + a controlled failover lab.

Quick answers
- Quota headers: yes — Redwood's public API surface currently returns headers similar to: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After on 429. We can enable those on the demo endpoints.
- Retry behavior: default SDKs will surface 429 to callers; we also provide an optional auto-retry layer that will back off with jitter. For Acme's demo we'll keep retries off to show explicit 429 behavior unless you want us to toggle it.
- Cost estimate: rough ballpark for the staged model variant we'll use: ~0.00085 USD per 1k tokens for generation (128-token request => ~0.00011 USD/request). We'll produce a calibrated cost-per-token after the sustained run.

Proposed test plan (staging + failover lab)
1) Baseline run (Sustained load) — baseline: 1k RPS, 30 minutes; collect P50/P95/P99, token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and per-request cost. (Run: 2 engineers, 24h prep, 6h execution + automated metrics ingestion)
2) Failover lab (controlled region outage) — simulate region failure in staging, validate cross-region routing + model-variant fallback. Success criteria: <2 minutes of elevated error rate, no silent data loss, and automatic traffic ramp to fallback region. (Run: SE + infra, requires temporary IP allowlist & test key)
3) Error-budget trigger test — inject 5% synthetic errors for 10 minutes to validate alerting and automatic fallback thresholds.
4) Rate-limit & retry test — burst clients to verify 429-first behavior and header correctness.
5) Cold-start scale tests — repeated scale-up cycles to capture cold-start percentiles.

Required items from Acme
- A technical contact to add a test key and allowlist IPs.
- A representative prompt set for the 128-token generation workload (Marcus can drop on the Drive link).

Schedule (tentative)
- Thu Nov 19: 10:00–11:30 PT — 30 minute demo + plan review; we run baseline tests afterward and share results within 48 hours.

Artifacts I pushed
- Failover runbook + assets (will attach as failover-demo-assets.zip)
- SLO spreadsheet populated with baseline pass/fail thresholds in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleReliabilityPlan
- HubSpot record updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-2026-045

If that looks good I'll schedule lab time and request the temporary keys/IP allowlist.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
